minutes.headline: Sewer Commission took no votes; it weighed partial-payment options for delinquent sewer bills and the Ray Pierce NPDES cost.
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission discussed filling vacancies, the expiring remote-meeting law, an estimated multi-year consultant cost for new permit requirements, and a proposal to let delinquent sewer customers make partial payments. The only vote was to adjourn. Staff were asked to check with the town collector on partial payments, and the permit item was held for the next meeting.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none was offered from the public. A commissioner used the slot to say the commission is seeking new members.
Second public comment call at the end; no public comment.

votes.motion: Motion to adjourn; seconded; Scott, Joe and the chair voted aye.

budget_items.topic: Ray Pierce consultant services for new permit requirements
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager gave a best-guess estimate of the consultant's fees for the permit work over four years, roughly a per-year share of that total.
A commissioner recalled an extra cost incurred on the pumps when two shut-offs proved too old, and suggested adding such items to the consultant's maintenance schedule.
The capital plan line can pay for any permit-related expenses not covered under the engineering line. The FY26 proposal was presented to the Finance Committee and described as clear.

budget_items.topic: Delinquent sewer bills and partial payments
budget_items.what_was_said: The Finance Committee had been concerned about the delinquency percentage. A commissioner argued that letting residents pay part of a bill online would bring in money that otherwise has to be collected through liens and attorneys.

budget_items.topic: Assistant to the business manager position
budget_items.what_was_said: The new hire is up for ratification that night and expected to start the following Monday.

decisions.decision: Commission will not opt into the AI minute-taking companion offered for town boards, preferring to keep its minute-taker.
Permit requirements discussion to be tabled to a future agenda; the business manager will ask the DPW director about scope.
The business manager will contact the town collector to ask whether partial online payments of sewer bills are possible.
Future agenda items: permit requirements, remote open-meeting law, commission vacancies and the rest of current business.
Commissioners agreed to consider another recruitment letter/mailing, possibly to a wider list, if the current effort yields few candidates.
Next meeting set for March 25 by Zoom; later meetings April 8, April 29 and May 13 to be hybrid at 7 p.m., with the April 29 time to be corrected.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission took no votes other than to adjourn.
The commission discussed letting delinquent sewer customers make partial online payments; the business manager will ask the town collector whether that is possible.
The Ray Pierce consultant cost for new permit requirements was estimated as a multi-year total; the item was tabled and the business manager will ask the DPW director about scope.
The commission declined the AI minute-taking companion offered to town boards and will keep its minute-taker.
Commissioners agreed to consider another recruitment mailing, possibly to a wider list, if the current effort yields few candidates for the vacancies.

why_it_matters: Partial payments could change how much overdue sewer revenue is collected without liens and attorneys, which bears on the delinquency rate the Finance Committee raised and on sewer rates.
The permit consultant cost is an estimate as heard and the item is tabled, so what permit compliance will add to sewer costs is not yet settled.
